name: weave
description: Run independent, adversarial AI participants via sub-agents or model CLIs to brainstorm, refine, plan, execute, architect, review, and synthesize.
author: Tony Narlock

name: rebase
description: Automated rebase onto trunk with conflict prediction, resolution, and quality gate verification.
author: Tony Narlock

name: changelog
description: Generate and maintain categorized changelog entries from branch commits and PR context.
author: Tony Narlock

name: tdd
description: TDD bug-fix workflow: reproduce bugs as failing tests, determine root cause, fix, and verify.
author: Tony Narlock

name: commit
description: Create git commits following project conventions with format enforcement and safety checks.
author: Tony Narlock

name: model-cli
description: Run prompts through individual AI CLIs — Antigravity/agy (Gemini), codex/GPT, and cursor/agent with fallback support.
author: Tony Narlock

name: pr
description: Manage gold-standard PR descriptions. Detects AI slop and verbose commits, resolving them via fixup commits and autosquash.
author: Tony Narlock

name: research
description: Study dependencies locally. Clones upstream repos and creates version-pinned worktrees matching your project's exact versions.
author: Tony Narlock

name: slop
description: Scan tracked files for AI slop and verbose noise, resolving each finding with atomic, verified commits.
author: Tony Narlock

name: tailwind
description: Detect and fix inconsistent spacing, margin/gap mixing, and padding asymmetry in Tailwind CSS layouts.
author: Tony Narlock

name: pytest-optimizer
description: Profile and optimize pytest suites. Ranks and applies safe speedups as verified, independent commits.
author: Tony Narlock

name: spike
description: Run no-commit spikes, strategy bakeoffs, or multi-round convergence in git worktrees. Tests ideas against quality gates and returns a commit-by-commit implementation plan.
author: Tony Narlock

name: action
description: Convert tickets to branches in isolated worktrees. Uses team branch conventions, lands gated commits, and supports parallel tickets.
author: Tony Narlock

name: lean
description: Writing discipline and cleanup tools for tight, slop-free prose and code.
author: Tony Narlock

name: double-check
description: Forces verification requests to return re-derived answers instead of diffs against prior turns. Includes an alignment tool for repairing chats.
author: Tony Narlock

name: release
description: Cut and bump releases with safe defaults (no automatic push/tag). Rolls out releases to downstream consumers with CI verification.
author: Tony Narlock

name: merge-pr
description: Merge PRs matching repo history conventions. Includes readiness checks, CI watching, stack detection, and automated rebasing.
author: Tony Narlock

name: business
description: Measure and report the business value of AI workflows with provenance-tagged data — metrics in engineer-hours and cycle time, never currency.
author: Tony Narlock

name: github-actions
description: Update GitHub Actions pins fleet-wide. Verifies tags, researches release notes, commits each action separately, and supersedes Dependabot PRs.
author: Tony Narlock

name: situate
description: Gain situational awareness before modifying code. Scans branches, PRs, tickets, and project conventions to orient the agent and verify the work required.
author: Tony Narlock

name: terraform
description: Upgrade Terraform and OpenTofu versions. Discovers every root module, moves provider constraints together because they combine across modules, and refreshes lock files.
author: Tony Narlock

name: ruff
description: Upgrade Ruff across repositories. Works out which new rules can fire against each repo's select list and lands one reviewed commit per rule, citing the upstream rule doc.
author: Tony Narlock

name: gh
description: File durable GitHub issues with reproductions, pinned links, and stripped PII. Enforces a markdown writing discipline reusable for any PR, comment, or ticket.
author: Tony Narlock

name: git-branch
description: Rebuild branch history into atomic commits (byte-identical), or reimplement from scratch using existing tests as the spec. Includes an interactive-rebase toolkit.
author: Tony Narlock

name: package-updater
description: Update dependencies and toolchains across repositories. Checks the supply-chain cooldown first, then commits toolchain, named bumps, and lockfile refreshes separately with release notes cited.
author: Tony Narlock

name: disk
description: Safely reclaim disk space. Classifies consumers as cache, redundant copy, or history, deleting only what is proven safe.
author: Tony Narlock

name: ticket
description: Manage work across trackers (Linear, Jira, GitHub, etc.) respecting each platform's native object graph. Drafts durable tickets focused on invariants.
author: Tony Narlock

name: respond
description: Screen review feedback from humans or bots before changing code. Verifies claims against facts and project decisions. Valid findings become gated, atomic commits; invalid ones get evidence-backed replies.
author: Tony Narlock

name: self-improvement
description: Mine local agent prompt history for how the skill catalog is really used, then land the changes that usage evidence supports.
author: Tony Narlock

name: agent-messaging
description: Message another running agent session — Claude Code or Codex — and verify who actually sent an incoming message.
author: Tony Narlock

name: skill-style
description: Hold SKILL.md files to a deletion test — a line stays only when its removal would change what the agent does — while frontmatter, code blocks, and sections survive verbatim.
author: Tony Narlock

name: scholar
description: Distil a checkable ontology from a codebase, a repository set, or a written corpus. Types, controlled vocabulary, cited and measured evidence.
author: Tony Narlock
